newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore blue chips pull back early on correction.
newsitem.headline: Singapore blue chips pull back early on correction.

text.p: Singapore blue chip shares were moderately lower early on Thursday, but Malaysian stocks clawied back the previous day's losses, dealers said.

"Institutions are reacting more or less to Greenspan's comments, but it's not like U.S. stocks are struggling," a local dealer said. He said the U.S. Federal Reserve chairman's warnings about inflation were a temporary and minor feature.

At 0240 GMT. the Straits Times Industrials Index was 8.87 points down to 2,207.20. But the UOB OTC index, tracking Malaysian issues, rebounded 11.21 points to 1,365.66 on abating concerns about changes to the settlement period.
In late Wednesday trade, rumours that the settlment period would be revised triggered selling in speculative counters.
Top gainers included Public Bank foreign shares, gaining Singapore $0.20 to S$3.46. Malaysia's Public Bank proposed bonus and rights issues to raise 842 million ringgit on Wednesday.
A broad section of blue chip stocks eased early, led by SPH foreign, down S$0.70 to S$27. Creative Technology fell S$0.30 to S$18.30 and SBS 500 eased S$0.15 to S$6.15.
Malaysian stocks dominated actives again with IGB up S$0.23 to S$1.06 and MBF Holdings down S$0.01 to S$0.97.
